report:
PASS applies solely to the complete restricted A–G theorem. I independently checked the current article, the historical restricted proof and first-moment-free supplement, and every reconstruction note n1–n7. No restricted proof depends on the excluded general L¹ coefficient theorem, unspecified E_env definitions, historical verdicts, candidate flags, or computational artifacts. The historical full-companion INCONCLUSIVE remains unchanged, and unrestricted S11 remains open.

A. Both residual constructions work. The article’s piecewise χ_L is increasing, convex and C¹ at its joining point; its unchanged singular tail differs from U by a finite constant. It satisfies dd^c U_L≥−ε_Lw, where ε_L→0, and U≤U_L≤0 with L¹ convergence to zero. The reconstruction’s q_L=L^α−(L−G_p)^α has the same ordinary type and curvature bound −αL^(α−1)w. The transverse boundary flux tends to zero, so these residuals have no point atom. Choosing the curvature loss below c−b supplies the displayed mutual-type strict witness even when c−b<α.

Canonical divisorial removal is valid for every rough competitor. Off D, subtracting bG_p leaves q~U. After adding a local quadratic, the bounded-above psh function extends canonically. The sharper nonclosed inequality survives: the extended positive Hessian has positive coefficient measures on D, whereas the smooth correction assigns D zero measure. Thus θ+dd^c v=b[D]+β+dd^c q, with β=(c−b)w1+aw2. Canonical equality follows from almost-everywhere equality; no subtraction of infinite pole values is used. Fiber averaging gives a positive curve measure (c−b)w+dd^c q̄ of total mass c−b. Negative mass excludes b>c; zero mass forces q̄ constant and contradicts q̄~U, excluding b=c. Empty types receive no numerical volume. The sublogarithmic residual is unbounded and cannot have an analytic ordinary type.

B. The calculation covers every rough fiber-dependent competitor. Set k=c−b>0 and choose the admissible reference U_L₀ with ε_L₀<k/2. For a closed K=C(w1+w2) dominating β, S=K+dd^c q and S₀=K+dd^c U_L₀ are closed positive cohomologous currents on the compact Kähler surface Y. Their potentials have bounded difference and are locally bounded outside the closed locally complete pluripolar divisor D. Consequently every hypothesis of the permitted comparison is established in degrees one and two and in both ordinary orders. It is never applied to a nonclosed current.

The separated reference has ⟨S₀²⟩=2C(Cw1+dd^c U_L₀)∧w2 and mass 2C². Degree-one comparison gives the full K-trace of ⟨S⟩. Since S−⟨S⟩=1_D S is positive and has zero strictly positive K-trace, it vanishes. Degree-two comparison gives ∫⟨S²⟩=∫K². With B=β−K, the actual extended measure is ⟨S²⟩+2B∧S+B². Each term is finite and has zero mass on D; bounded locality identifies the expression off D, hence globally. Distributional Stokes yields M(v)=∫β²+2∫q dd^cβ=2∫aσ, where σ=kw+dd^c q̄ is positive of mass k. This proves positive finite masses and both global bounds. It uses only L¹ pairing with smooth forms, not a nonlinear first moment.

Both extremizing constructions are actual same-type potentials. In the article, smooth positive ζ_j of mass k are paired with sufficiently small-curvature U_L_j. In n2, σ_j=(k−η_j)ξ_j+(η_jw+dd^c q_L_j), where the second positive summand has mass η_j→0. Thus σ_j→kδ_x and M(v_j)→2ka(x), including when x=p. Taking x at the extrema proves R_−=2k min a and R_+=2k max a. Finally ∫G_p dd^c a=a(p)−∫aw gives exactly the asserted original-background affine formula. The historical supplement’s raw-U range c≥α is respected; its application when k<α uses the admissible U_L₀ reference, whose hypotheses were checked separately.

C. The chosen r₀ is genuinely admissible, so its product pullback gives the claimed Θ-psh ambient potential. Θ is strictly positive, and dΘ≠0 when a is nonconstant. The generic Lelong number along Y₀ is zero because the reference is locally bounded on its generic locus. Near D_Z, u_Z=b log|z|²−T^α+O(1), with T=−log|z|². A germ of transverse order j has radial integral comparable to ∫exp(−(j+1−sb)T+sT^α)dT. It converges precisely when j+1>sb. At equality it diverges, so the coefficient is floor(sb), including every integer boundary weight with the stipulated no-extra-factor-2 convention. Factoring a general germ and using a nonzero leading tangential coefficient establishes both necessity and sufficiency.

Restricting these actual ambient principal ideals gives O_Y₀(−floor(sb)D). Their orders on every smooth compact modification are floor(sb)ord_E(π*D); the defining limit therefore equals b ord_E(π*D). This establishes the entire intrinsic trace system through ambient ideal restrictions. It does not assert multiplier-ideal pullback commutation. The residual has trivial ideals at all real weights while remaining unbounded.

D. For q_L, angular integration with T=−G_p gives w=e^(−T)dT and dG_p∧d^cG_p=(1−e^(−T))dT. The positive curve measure Cw+dd^c q_L has density (C−α(L+T)^(α−1))e^(−T)+α(1−α)(L+T)^(α−2)(1−e^(−T)), mass C and no atom. Thus its actual separated closed square has full mass 2C². Multiplication by −q_L gives the positive first-moment tail 2Cα(1−α)T^(2α−2)dT. Finiteness is exactly α<1/2; at α=1/2 the divergence is (C/2)log R for a T-cutoff R. The article’s shifted tail has the same threshold. No energy or first-moment hypothesis enters A–C.

E. Smooth gauges preserve actual currents, finite-level products and their extensions, competitor classes, and all real-weight ideals. For a pure modification, adding a pulled-back local quadratic makes the upstairs potential psh. Descent on the biholomorphic complement has a local upper bound by properness; canonical removal and the coefficient-measure argument retain the exact downstairs smooth-background inequality. Ordinary comparisons extend canonically. Pullback and descent are inverse, including pole values. For modifications, the sharper pullback inequality follows by the same extension argument; n1 also supplies a valid decreasing local approximation proof. Locality on the biholomorphic complements and zero mass on analytic sets prove the actual pushforward law, upstairs finiteness, and equality of both optimized masses. Intrinsic trace transport means total transforms of the original restricted ambient ideals, followed by composition of modifications.

Both point-blowup witnesses are valid. The author’s negative exceptional curvature has the required vertical sign; the displayed Schur-complement estimate proves positivity after choosing the neighborhood and then the parameter small. In n5, the cutoff logarithm pulls back near E to log|s|²+log(1+|ξ|²), so its Hessian is [E]+η with η smooth and positive tangentially on E. The form επ*ω+δη is strictly positive near E, remains positive in the inner punctured region, and is positive on the cutoff annulus for δM<ε. The resulting genuine witness is at most π*r plus a constant and acquires an exceptional pole.

Conversely, mutual ordinary equivalence forces boundedness near E. A hypothetical strict witness can be restricted genuinely to E: subtract local quadratics whose constant Hessians lie below the smooth lower bound, with positive tangent coefficient. The restricted curve Hessian is then strictly positive, contradicting its zero integral by Stokes. Thus positive preserved lower mass supplies no mutual strict witness on this blowup. Exceptional curvature subtraction and invariance for arbitrary upstairs Gauduchon densities are not asserted.

F. Both independent all-test proofs are sound with D_μ(T)=∫sqrt(T²/μ)μ and V_μ equal to the square of the infimum quotient. In the article, Poisson solvability gives Ω=gw1+aw2=β+dd^c f with Ω²=Vμ. Stokes and matrix arithmetic–geometric mean prove the lower bound for every positive dd^c-closed test. The closed positive T=Ω/a attains it. In n6, fiber integration of an arbitrary mixed test gives a positive constant vertical average κ; determinant positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz give D²≤2AκH, while the numerator is kκ+A. The identity (A−kκ)²≥0 proves the same unrestricted bound. Both give V_μ(β)=2k/H, separately from V_μ(θ)=2c/H. The dependence on m and distinction from R_+ follow directly.

For fixed real d and smooth first-factor e, H_s′=∫em/a_s² and D_μ(T_s)=sqrt(V_s)H_s. Direct differentiation gives (sqrt(V_s))′=−[d+(V_s/2)H_s′]/[sqrt(V_s)H_s], exactly the claimed minimizing-test pairing. Uniform positivity on each compact segment justifies differentiation and integration. With signed d,e this is a signed subtraction identity; it is not a derivative of R_+.

G. The author’s U_31 has ε_31≈0.315336<3/8. The reconstruction’s alternative q_16=8−(16−G_p)^(3/4) has curvature loss exactly 3/8 and gives a strict lower bound (3/8)(w1+w2). Both are valid mutual-type references. The height distribution gives min a=1, max a=3 and H=(log 3)/2. Hence R_−=3/2, R_+=9/2, V_μ(β)=3/log 3 and V_μ(θ)=4/log 3, with every trace equal to (1/4)ord_E(π*D). The residual first moment is infinite. The point-blowup conclusions follow from E. The target backgrounds are genuinely nonclosed; the auxiliary K is closed.

Dependency audit: the supplied note graph is acyclic: n1 has no note parents; n2←n1; n3←n1; n4←n1,n2,n3; n5←n1,n2,n3; n6←n2; n7←n1,…,n6. Every listed parent is available and checked; some edges are unnecessary but harmless. At the mathematical level, canonical local arguments use premise 2 and permitted elementary foundations; B additionally uses premises 0,1,3,4; C uses A and transverse integrability; D uses the separated reference; E uses canonical arguments, B and C; F uses only permitted sphere Poisson solvability, Stokes and matrix inequalities; G uses A–F. Premise 5 concerns attribution, not an indispensable calculation dependency.

Fresh primary checks confirm the auxiliary product facts in [BEGZ](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf). Existing definitions and divisorial/modification laws retain [BGL’s credit](https://d-nb.info/1374372846/34). Companion bounded-residual trace constructions, floor ideals, subtraction mechanisms and the local exceptional-curve obstruction also retain their stated credit. Their unrelated coefficient and envelope assertions are outside this proof graph. The historical report’s verdict and repeated short evidence fragments are not adopted as proof; its unresolved full scope remains unresolved.

Harmless wording corrections are already incorporated in the current version: b=0 denotes the identically zero divisorial term, only the target backgrounds are described as nonclosed, d and e are declared, and pure-pullback claims are confined to the stated masses and trace transport. Logarithmic moment divergence refers to the T-cutoff. No substantial repair of an A–G proof was required. This restricted PASS establishes no priority claim, unrestricted S11 completion, general Hermitian strict-type criterion, exceptional-subtraction invariance, or multiplier-ideal pullback theorem.

passages.statement: On a compact Kahler manifold, the non-pluripolar product of finitely many closed positive (1,1) currents of total degree at most the dimension is well defined and has finite mass.
passages.quote: On a compact Kahler manifold, the non-pluripolar product of finitely many closed positive (1,1) currents of total degree at most the dimension is well defined and has finite mass.

passages.statement: On a compact Kahler manifold, two tuples of cohomologous closed positive (1,1) currents with small unbounded locus satisfy the ordinary-singularity-order comparison of the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products: if every current of the first tuple is less singular, its product class minus the second product class is pseudoeffective. Small unbounded locus means local boundedness outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set.
passages.quote: On a compact Kahler manifold, two tuples of cohomologous closed positive (1,1) currents with small unbounded locus satisfy the ordinary-singularity-order comparison of the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products: if every current of the first tuple is less singular, its product class minus the second product class is pseudoeffective. Small unbounded locus means local boundedness outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set.

passages.statement: For a closed pluripolar set A in a complex manifold, a psh function on its complement which is locally bounded above near A extends uniquely to a genuine canonical psh function. Genuine psh functions have positive distributional complex Hessian, and their pullbacks under holomorphic maps are psh, possibly identically minus infinity on a component.

passages.statement: A well-defined non-pluripolar product of closed positive (1,1)-currents on a complex manifold is closed (BEGZ Theorem 1.8).

Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ for psh φ; for locally bounded potentials off a closed locally complete pluripolar set, a well-defined non-pluripolar product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement (BEGZ §1.2).

Locally, ⟨dd^cφ⟩=1_{φ>−∞}dd^cφ for psh φ; for locally bounded potentials off a closed locally complete pluripolar set, a well-defined non-pluripolar product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford–Taylor product from its complement (BEGZ §1.2).

On a compact complex manifold with BMP, the lower and upper volumes of a quasi-closed positive (1,1)-current are the finite top-mass infimum and supremum in its dd^c-class and ordinary singularity type. Effective real divisor addition and smooth compact modification pullback preserve both volumes (BGL, Definition 3.1; Proposition 3.3).
